# Reorderable

A list the user puts in order: recipe steps, a queue, favorites. Each row has a drag handle, a 44px target on a touch screen. Dragging it moves the row, the other rows make room, and holding it near the top or bottom edge scrolls the list or the page. A touch that starts anywhere else on a row scrolls as usual.

```tsx
import { Reorderable } from "@/registry/ouro/components/ouro/reorderable/reorderable";
```

## Example

```tsx
<Reorderable
  label="Steps"
  items={steps.map((step) => ({ id: step.id, label: step.title, content: <Item title={step.title} description={step.text} /> }))}
  onReorder={(ids) => setSteps(ids.map((id) => steps.find((step) => step.id === id)!))}
/>
```

## Usage

From the keyboard, focus a handle and press Space to pick the row up, the up and down arrow keys to move it, Space to drop it and Escape to cancel, which puts it back. Moving focus away drops it where it is. Every step is announced to screen readers with the row's position ("Sear the ribs moved. Position 3 of 7."), and each spoken string is a prop with an English default.

The list shows the new order at once and keeps it; `onReorder` reports it, once per drop. With reduced motion the other rows jump out of the way instead of sliding.

## Use instead when

- Use `ItemGroup` instead for a list whose order the user does not change, and `Resizable` to change sizes, not order.

## Props

Type: `ReorderableProps`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `canceledLabel` | `string` | `"{label} put back. Position {n} of {total}."` | Announced when a move is cancelled and the row goes back. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Layout only: margins, or a height with `overflow-auto` (`max-h-80 overflow-auto`) to scroll the list in place. Appearance classes warn in development. |
| `droppedLabel` | `string` | `"{label} dropped. Position {n} of {total}."` | Announced when a row is dropped. |
| `handleLabel` | `string` | `"Reorder {label}"` | Each handle's accessible name; `{label}` is the row's label. |
| `instructionsLabel` | `string` | `"Press Space to pick up. Use the arrow keys to move, Space to drop, and Escape to cancel."` | How to use a handle from the keyboard, read after its name. |
| `items` (required) | `readonly ReorderableItem[]` |  | The rows, in order: `{ id, label, content }`. Pass them in a new order to change the order from outside. |
| `label` (required) | `string` |  | Names the list for screen readers, such as "Steps". Always required. |
| `movedLabel` | `string` | `"{label} moved. Position {n} of {total}."` | Announced on each move with the arrow keys. |
| `onReorder` | `((ids: string[], move: ReorderableMove) => void)` |  | Called once when the user drops a row in a new place, with every id in the new order and the move. The list already shows the new order; save it, or keep it in state. |
| `pickedUpLabel` | `string` | `"{label} picked up. Position {n} of {total}."` | Announced when a row is picked up; `{label}`, `{n}` (its position) and `{total}` are filled in. |

## Don't use

These are not props. Passing one fails the type check with the fix in the error, and in development a console message names the fix.

- `axis`: Not a prop. Reorderable is a vertical list.
- `children`: Not a prop. Rows are data, with their content in `content`: `items={[{ id: "1", label: "Sear", content: <Item title="Sear" /> }]}`.
- `onChange`: Not a prop. Ouro UI uses `onReorder`: `onReorder={(ids) => save(ids)}`.
- `onDragEnd`: Not a prop. Ouro UI uses `onReorder`: `onReorder={(ids) => save(ids)}`.
- `renderItem`: Not a prop. Each row's `content` is what it shows: `items={[{ id: "1", label: "Sear", content: <Item title="Sear" /> }]}`.
- `values`: Not a prop. Ouro UI uses `items`: `items={steps.map((step) => ({ id: step.id, label: step.title }))}`.

## `className` is for layout only

Pass margins, width and grid placement (`mt-4`, `w-full`, `col-span-2`). Your classes always win over Ouro UI's: each component merges `className` last with `cn` (tailwind-merge), so a class that conflicts with the component's own replaces it.

Appearance comes from props, not classes. In development, a class that sets appearance logs one warning per component instance, naming the prop to use instead. A class sets appearance when, after its variants (`hover:`, `sm:`) and any `!` are removed, it starts with `bg-`, `text-`, `border-`, `rounded-`, `shadow-`, `font-`, `ring-`, `from-`, `via-`, `to-`, `fill-` or `stroke-`, or is `border`, `rounded`, `shadow` or `ring`, or has a `dark:` variant. Text wrapping, overflow and table layout classes (`text-wrap`, `text-ellipsis`, `border-collapse`) are layout and do not warn.

Alignment classes (`text-center`) warn too: set alignment on a parent element.

## Types

### `ReorderableItem`

One row of a `Reorderable`.

```ts
interface ReorderableItem {
  /** Identifies the row; `onReorder` reports the new order as these ids. Unique in the list. */
  id: string;
  /** Names the row for its handle ("Reorder Sear the ribs") and in announcements. It is the row's content too, unless you pass `content`. */
  label: string;
  /** What the row shows, in place of the label: an `Item`, or any content. */
  content?: ReactNode;
}
```

### `ReorderableMove`

The move `onReorder` reports: the row's id and its position before and after, counting from 0.

```ts
interface ReorderableMove {
  id: string;
  from: number;
  to: number;
}
```
